platform: Pure Python (20 stochastic replications) / exported AnyLogic JAR via subprocess (full)
upstream_reference: Argonne National Laboratory helium market ABM (AnyLogic), technical report 2022
calibration_sources: Massol & Rifaat (2018) demand elasticity

key_equations: per replication: shock_i = shock x exp(N(0, 0.15)); eps_i = eps + N(0, 0.05)

limitations: No agent heterogeneity, hoarding or contract dynamics; noise is parametric, not emergent
license_notes: AnyLogic Professional required for the full model; the reduction is repository code.
description: Argonne Helium ABM (AnyLogic): agent-based model of contemporary helium market dynamics developed at Argonne National Laboratory. Simulates heterogeneous producer, distributor, and end-user agents to capture emergent market behavior — hoarding, spot price spikes, contract renegotiation, and cascading shortfalls — under supply disruption scenarios triggered by Strait of Hormuz closure.

platform: Pure Python (reduction) / Julia MPSGE.jl + JuMP via juliacall or subprocess (full)
upstream_reference: MPSGE.jl (julia-mpsge) with a GTAP v10+ database
calibration_sources: Hamilton (2003; 2009 Brookings) oil-to-GDP elasticity (-0.025 pp per 1% oil shock)
Kilian (2008 RES) oil supply shock GDP response
Blanchard & Gali (2007); Kilian & Zhou (2022) oil-to-CPI pass-through (0.04 pp per 1%)
Baffes (2007); FAO (2022) fertilizer pass-through
Massol & Rifaat (2018) helium market response
UN-Water (2024) water shortage GDP impact
IMF Regional Economic Outlook Middle East (2022) terms-of-trade responses
Anderson & van Wincoop (2003) gravity trade elasticity -0.4
trade-cost to capex pass-through 0.3
key_equations: gdp_impact_pct = scaler(duration) x sum_c e_gdp,c x shock_c
cpi_inflation_pct = clip(scaler, 0.5, 1.2) x sum_c e_cpi,c x shock_c
consumption = gdp - 0.4 x cpi; welfare = consumption; wage = 0.6 x cpi + 0.5 x gdp; rate = 0.5 x cpi + 0.25 x gdp
regional rows = headline response x per-region, per-commodity multipliers (REGIONAL_GDP_MULTIPLIERS / REGIONAL_CPI_MULTIPLIERS)
regime = long_run (scaler linear in duration); capex shock = (trade_cost_multiplier - 1) x 100 x 0.3
bilateral flow change = -0.4 x (trade_cost_multiplier - 1) x 100 x Hormuz exposure; terms of trade = coef_r x oil shock
limitations: Headline gdp_impact_pct is the OECD/US-calibrated reference economy of the kernel, not a world aggregate; gdp_impact_pct_world_weighted is the PPP-share-weighted mean of the regional rows
Linear in shocks; no general-equilibrium feedback, trade rebalancing or dynamics beyond the duration scaler
No factor markets, sectoral production structure or GTAP data in the reduction

display_name: Baumeister-Hamilton oil-shock SVAR (2019 AER), reduced form
platform: Pure Python (reduction); upstream MATLAB/R SVAR code not run
upstream_reference: Baumeister & Hamilton (2019), 'Structural Interpretation of Vector Autoregressions with Incomplete Identification', AER 109(5). Not a Federal Reserve model; the 'Fed workhorse' label in earlier drafts refers to the framework's use in Fed policy analysis.
calibration_sources: Baumeister & Hamilton (2019 AER, Table 3) shock-type multipliers and FEVD shares
Kilian (2009 AER) IRF magnitudes and decay
Taylor (1993) rule with conservative inflation coefficient 0.5
Okun's law coefficient -0.5
macro_kernel headline elasticities (Hamilton 2003/2009; Blanchard & Gali 2007)
key_equations: peak_gdp = kernel_gdp(oil shock) x m_gdp[shock_type]; peak_cpi = kernel_cpi(oil shock) x m_cpi[shock_type]
gdp_q = peak_gdp x 0.85^q; cpi_q = peak_cpi x 0.75^q
ffr_0 = 0.5 x cpi_0; ffr_q = 0.9 x ffr_{q-1} + 0.5 x (cpi_q - cpi_{q-1}); hence peak CPI = 2 x peak FFR by construction
unemployment_q = -0.5 x gdp_q; hence peak unemployment = 0.5 x |peak GDP| by construction
limitations: Not an estimated SVAR: IRFs are geometric decays of kernel peaks with fixed multipliers, so CPI/FFR and GDP/unemployment ratios are identities, not independent results
ZLB reported as a flag only
license_notes: Repository code; upstream replication files are the authors'.
description: Baumeister-Hamilton (2019 AER) oil-shock SVAR, closed-form reduction. Not a Federal Reserve model: the historical 'Fed workhorse' label refers to the framework's use in Fed policy analysis. Decomposes oil shocks into supply, demand, and speculative components and traces reduced-form impulse responses of GDP, CPI, the federal funds rate, and unemployment over a 2–8 quarter short-run horizon. Peak CPI = 2 x peak FFR and peak unemployment = 0.5 x |peak GDP| hold by construction (Taylor coefficient 0.5, Okun coefficient -0.5); see outputs['_reduced_form_equations'].

dP/P = supply_loss_pct / (eps_s - (eps_d - 0.5 x substitute_availability))
peak_price = 80 x (1 + dP/P) + rerouting_wedge + insurance_wedge; linear decay to baseline over the disruption
limitations: No regional energy balances, fuel substitution across carriers, or inventory dynamics; single global Brent price

description: POLES-JRC (Prospective Outlook on Long-term Energy Systems) — European Commission JRC partial-equilibrium global energy model. Covers all energy carriers with regional detail; used here for oil and LNG price trajectories and trade-flow impacts under Strait of Hormuz disruption.
